content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion 1 contradicts inclusion criterion 7a",
      "quote": "Neutrophil count at or above 1200 /mm3.",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "Inclusion criterion 7a requires neutrophil count ≥ 1500/mm3, but exclusion criterion 1 excludes subjects with neutrophil count ≥ 1200/mm3. This creates an impossible window (1200-1499) where subjects are neither eligible nor ineligible, likely causing confusion and amendments.",
      "fix": "Change exclusion criterion to 'Neutrophil count below 1500/mm3' or align with inclusion threshold."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 4c is ambiguous and likely erroneous",
      "quote": "Documented disease progression in any lesion that was previously radiated in order to serve as a target lesion.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The wording suggests that a previously radiated lesion must have documented progression to serve as a target lesion, but it is unclear if this applies to all target lesions or only those radiated. This could lead to misinterpretation and protocol amendments.",
      "fix": "Clarify: 'Any lesion that was previously radiated must have documented progression to be considered measurable and eligible as a target lesion.'"
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 5 requires biopsy but allows unsafe biopsy with Medical Monitor discussion",
      "quote": "If the Investigator believes it is unsafe to perform a biopsy, the subject may be considered eligible after discussion with the Medical Monitor if tissue and/or prior assessments are available to determine programmed death-ligand 1 expression.",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The criterion is vague about what constitutes 'unsafe' and what 'prior assessments' are acceptable, potentially leading to inconsistent enrollment decisions and amendments.",
      "fix": "Define specific safety criteria for biopsy and specify acceptable alternative tissue sources."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion 15 is overly broad and may exclude asymptomatic patients",
      "quote": "Known or suspected active infection with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 virus.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "4.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The criterion excludes any subject with 'suspected' COVID-19, which could be interpreted broadly and exclude patients with mild symptoms or those who have recovered, leading to unnecessary screening burden and potential enrollment delays.",
      "fix": "Specify that exclusion applies to confirmed active infection or symptomatic disease requiring treatment."
    },
    {
      "title": "Secondary endpoint includes 'Blood concentrations of CMP-001 or its metabolites' but PK objective is only for CMP-001",
      "quote": "Blood concentrations of CMP-001 or its metabolites",
      "page": 33,
      "section": "2.2.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The secondary objective (Section 2.1.2) only mentions 'PK profile of CMP-001', not metabolites. Including metabolites in the endpoint may require additional assays not specified in the PK analysis plan.",
      "fix": "Align endpoint with objective: 'Blood concentrations of CMP-001' or update objective to include metabolites."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion 3b requires PD within 12 weeks of last dose, but confirmatory assessment may be baseline if within 30 days",
      "quote": "Have PD (according to RECIST v1.1) within 12 weeks of the last dose of a PD-1 blocking antibody",
      "page": 38,
      "section": "4.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The 12-week window for PD after last dose is restrictive and may exclude patients who progress later but are still refractory. The confirmatory assessment allowance is helpful but the initial window may cause enrollment delays.",
      "fix": "Consider extending the window or allowing documented progression at any time after PD-1 therapy if refractory."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion 6 requires recovery to Grade 1 but allows exceptions, yet note adds adrenal insufficiency testing",
      "quote": "Not fully recovered from AEs (to Grade 1 or less [per CTCAE v5.0], with the exception of persistent adverse events or sequelae, eg, vitiligo, alopecia, hypothyroidism, diabetes mellitus, and adrenal and/or pituitary insufficiency)",
      "page": 39,
      "section": "4.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The note requires diagnostic tests for adrenal insufficiency in certain subjects, but the criterion itself is vague about what constitutes 'not fully recovered' for endocrine AEs, potentially leading to inconsistent application.",
      "fix": "Clarify that endocrine AEs managed with replacement therapy are considered recovered if stable."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exploratory endpoint includes itRECIST but no reference to Appendix F in the text",
      "quote": "Response in injected and noninjected target lesions per intratumoral Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors (itRECIST, Appendix F, Goldmacher-2020)",
      "page": 34,
      "section": "2.2.3 Exploratory Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The endpoint references Appendix F, but the protocol text does not include the appendix or a summary of itRECIST criteria, which may lead to inconsistent assessment.",
      "fix": "Include Appendix F or provide a summary of itRECIST criteria in the protocol."
    }
  ]
}
